Where does the Agentic OS observability increment stand?

Long image

A

Answer

The increment is a read-only observability layer over the tool inventory: a markdown vault holds each tool's state, the Markdown Engine reads it, and Jarvis shows it. Four of eight tickets are resolved, and the vault note schema (ticket 05) now gates every remaining one.

  1. The tool matrix owns identity and classification; the vault owns operational state.1
  2. Nothing acts in this increment: server code is limited to read-only routes that report state.
  3. Jarvis is built from four FounderOS parts, copied and adapted, about 20k lines.2
  4. Tool state is three separate axes, not one ladder: status, active and health.3

Applies toState of .scratch/agentic-os-observability on 2026-11-25spec only, building is a separate effort

1

What are the parts, and who owns which data?

Diagram structure
  • Partner partner
  • Tool matrix matrix
  • Markdown vault vault
  • Markdown Engine engine
  • Jarvis jarvis
  • Framework map fmap
  • FounderOS founderos
  • Obsidian obsidian
  • matrix → vault · generates identity
  • vault → matrix · writes back state
  • partner → vault · commits moves
  • vault → engine · notes
  • engine → jarvis · read-only routes
  • founderos → jarvis · copied parts
  • jarvis → fmap · links or embeds
  • matrix → fmap · builds
  • vault → obsidian · optional viewer
  1. Tool matrix ↗

    Owns id, name, kind, tier, cluster and needs. It stays the primary inventory, in this repo.

  2. Markdown vault ↗

    A git repo, also opened as an Obsidian vault. Notes are generated from the matrix and checked against it. The vault owns status, declared activity, notes and links.

  3. Markdown Engine ↗

    Reads the vault, round-trips markdown and HTML, and serves read-only routes. Health is computed live here and is never stored.

  4. Jarvis ↗

    The front end, in a new repo on the FounderOS stack. Tool status shows here only.

  5. Framework map ↗

    Its design is not changed (open–closed). Jarvis links to it or embeds it.

  6. FounderOS ↗

    Export, not merge: modules are copied with the MIT notice, or re-implemented where they are tied to business domains.

The write-back path is not designed yet

The dashed arrow from the vault to the tool matrix is ticket 06. Column or sidecar file, direction, trigger and mismatch reporting are all open.

RequirementWhat it rules in or out

Open–closed framework mapThe map stays its own build. Status in the 3D map is deferred.
Split ownershipThe matrix owns identity. Markdown owns operational state and writes it back for the map to read.
Vault is a git repoObsidian is an optional viewer, not a dependency.
Read-only serverRoutes may report state. Anything that acts waits for the next increment.
Four co-opted partsKnowledge Visualizer, brain observatory, skills catalogue, Usage.
Galaxy mappingA galaxy is a tier, a constellation is a cluster, a star is a tool.
Runs on LinuxWorkstation migration is expected in early December 2026.

These nine points were settled at charting and are not tickets.1

4

How does a tool's state become what Jarvis shows?

Diagram structure
  • Tool in matrix tool
  • Implemented? impl
  • Health check passes? check
  • Standing and running? run
  • Active act
  • No state none
  • Attention att
  • Idle idle
  • check → att · no
  • check → run · yes
  • impl → check · yes
  • impl → none · no
  • run → act · yes
  • run → idle · no
  • tool → impl
AxisValuesWho sets it, and where
Statuscatalogued → implemented → retiredA partner, by commit to the tool note
Activeyes or no, standing tools onlyA probe, or a partner's declaration in the note
Healthpass, fail, not checkedThe check, live; stored nowhere
  • Implemented needs four things: findable, available, invokable and usable.
  • A health check re-runs the first three. A check that cannot run shows attention with the reason "not checked".
  • Catalogued and retired tools show no state. A retired tool may return to implemented, never to catalogued.
  • A cluster or tier has no status. It shows counts, and attention when any of its tools does.
  • A standing tool not seen active for 30 days is flagged for a partner. Nothing is demoted automatically.

  1. 05 Vault note schema ↗

    The only open ticket with no open blocker. Settles note kinds, folders, the identity key, frontmatter, and how generated sections are fenced from hand-written ones.

  2. 06 State write-back ↗

    Settles how vault state reaches the matrix and how matrix changes reach the vault, without either overwriting the other.

  3. 07 Visualizer data model ↗

    Settles entity kinds, which edge kinds count as cross-references, which sections stay, and what the graph metrics tell a partner.

  4. 08 Jarvis static layout ↗

    A static prototype with mock data: panel positions and the path from a star to its note and its place in the framework map.

The dashed arrows are a reading, not a recorded dependency

The map names the spec as the destination. It lists spec assembly as not yet specified, including which repo the spec lands in.
